### 3. COURSE SUMMARY

### 4. COURSE-SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (CO)

By the end of this program, students should have the following knowledge, skills, and

values:

 CO1: Explain ethical hacking principles, cyber laws, reconnaissance and information

gathering.

 CO2: Perform network scanning, enumeration and vulnerability assessment using

professional tools.

 CO3: Analyze and assess web, wireless, cloud, mobile and IoT security vulnerabilities.

 CO4: Apply penetration testing methodologies using Metasploit and related security tools.

 CO5: Evaluate vulnerabilities, prioritize remediation and prepare professional assessment

reports.

19. Metasploit Framework and Advanced Exploitation Techniques

Labs

1. Setting up an Ethical Hacking Lab Environment using Virtualization -VirtualBox/VMware

and Installing Kali Linux/Parrot OS

2. Passive Information Gathering using OSINT Framework, Whois, DNS Lookup, and

Google Dorking Techniques

3. Active Reconnaissance: Network Scanning with Nmap for Host Discovery, Port

Scanning, and Service Detection

4. Vulnerability Analysis using OpenVAS or Nessus to Identify Security Weaknesses in

Target Systems

5. Enumeration of Services and Users using Tools like Netcat, Telnet, and SNMPWalk

6. Password Cracking using Tools like Hydra for Online Attacks and John Ripper for Offline

Cracking

7. Exploiting System Vulnerabilities using Metasploit Framework -Auxiliary Modules,

Exploits, Payloads

8. Web Application Vulnerability Assessment using Burp Suite Proxy to Intercept and

Analyze Web Traffic

9. SQL Injection Attacks: Identifying and Exploiting SQL Injection Vulnerabilities in Web

Applications using Tools like SQLmap

10. Wireless Network Penetration Testing using Aircrack-ng Suite to Capture and Crack

WEP/WPA/WPA2 Keys

11. Cloud Security Assessment: Exploring AWS/Azure Security Configurations and

Identifying Common Misconfigurations using Command Line Tools or Web Consoles

12. API Security Testing using Postman or OWASP ZAP to Test for Common API

Vulnerabilities such as Broken Authentication and Authorization

11. Software/Tools Used:

The course utilizes industry-standard ethical hacking and penetration testing software to

provide practical exposure to vulnerability assessment, network security, web application

security, cloud security, API security, wireless security, malware analysis, and digital

forensics. Students perform laboratory experiments using Kali Linux, Parrot Security OS,

Oracle VirtualBox, VMware Workstation, Nmap, Wireshark, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP,

Metasploit Framework, OpenVAS, Nessus Essentials, SQLmap, Hydra, John the Ripper,

Aircrack-ng, Netcat, SNMPWalk, Postman, DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, bWAPP, AWS

Free Tier, Microsoft Azure, Lynis, Sysinternals Suite, Autopsy, Volatility Framework,

PEStudio, Visual Studio Code, Git, and Python. These tools enable students to develop

practical skills in ethical hacking, penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, digital

forensics, and secure system analysis.

12. Hardware/Devices Used:

The course requires modern desktop or laptop computers with multi-core Intel Core i5/i7 or

AMD Ryzen processors, a minimum of 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD storage, and hardware

virtualization support (Intel VT-x/AMD-V) to execute multiple virtual machines and

penetration testing tools efficiently. The laboratory utilizes managed network switches,

wireless routers, external USB Wi-Fi adapters supporting monitor mode and packet

injection, Raspberry Pi and ESP32 development boards for IoT security experiments,

Android smartphones, external storage devices for digital forensics, multimedia projectors,

and reliable high-speed Internet connectivity. Optional infrastructure such as firewall

appliances (Fortinet/pfSense), NAS devices, and forensic write blockers may be used for

advanced security, network defense, and digital forensic investigations.

13. Proposed Case Studies:

Enterprise Network Vulnerability Assessment

 Perform reconnaissance, network scanning, service enumeration, and vulnerability

assessment of a simulated enterprise network using Nmap, Nessus, and OpenVAS. Analyze

identified vulnerabilities and recommend remediation measures.

Web Application Penetration Testing

metadata.department: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Computer Science and Engineering, Information Technology

chunks.text:
 Conduct a comprehensive security assessment of a deliberately vulnerable web application

(DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, or bWAPP) to identify SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting

(XSS), Broken Authentication, and other OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities using Burp Suite,

SQLmap, and OWASP ZAP.

Wireless Network Security Assessment

 Evaluate the security of a wireless network by analyzing Wi-Fi protocols

(WEP/WPA/WPA2/WPA3), performing controlled wireless security assessments using

Aircrack-ng, and recommending secure wireless configurations.

Cloud Infrastructure Security Assessment

 Assess the security configuration of cloud resources hosted on AWS or Microsoft Azure by

identifying common misconfigurations, access control weaknesses, exposed storage

services, and implementing cloud security best practices based on the shared responsibility

model.

Incident Response and Vulnerability Management

 Simulate a cyber incident involving malware infection or unauthorized access. Perform

vulnerability assessment, analyze attack vectors, prioritize vulnerabilities using CVSS,

prepare a professional Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) report,

and recommend mitigation and incident response strategies.

14. Advanced Research Topics:

1. AI-Assisted Ethical Hacking and Automated Penetration Testing

Applying Artificial Intelligence to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery,

exploitation, and penetration testing.

2. Large Language Models (LLMs) for Vulnerability Discovery and Exploit

Analysis

Leveraging LLMs to identify software vulnerabilities, analyze exploits, generate

secure code, and assist security analysts.

3. Cloud-Native Security and Kubernetes Penetration Testing

Research on securing cloud-native applications, containerized environments,

Kubernetes clusters, and cloud infrastructure.

4. Zero-Day Vulnerability Detection using Machine Learning

Developing intelligent machine learning and deep learning models to detect

previously unknown cyber threats and zero-day attacks.

5. IoT and Industrial IoT (IIoT) Security Assessment

Investigating security vulnerabilities, penetration testing techniques, and defense

mechanisms for IoT and industrial control systems.

15. Attendance Policy:

1. At least 75% attendance in the course is mandatory

2. A maximum of 5% shall be allowed under medical grounds and 5% on representing the

University on official events outside like sports, hackathons, NCC, NSS etc.

3. Students with less than 65% of attendance shall be prevented from writing the final

assessment.

16. Academic Dishonesty & Plagiarism:

Plagiarism is "to offer work or ideas from another source as one's own, with or without

authorization of the source author(s), directly by verbatim copying or by usage of any AI

software" (i.e., with or without permission from the original author). In certain cases,

authorization might be provided for the usage of other sources through written permission

metadata.department: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Computer Science and Engineering, Information Technology

chunks.text:
may not be considered as plagiarism. It is a serious academic offence which should be

avoided; the following method will be adopted to evaluate plagiarism in submitted

documents including assignments, material, class test content and other similar academic

documents.

 Level 1: Similarities up to 10% - Student will be asked to revise the document

and resubmit for evaluation, once chance will be provided to revise.

 Level 2: Similarities above 10% to 20%- Student will be warned and one chance

will be provided to revise the document and resubmit.

 Level 3: Similarities above 20%: If the plagiarism level is more than 20%

student will get a Fail grade.
